description: ORDER-N IMPASSE ESCALATION — domain-agnostic meta-cognition. When a faculty was already TAUGHT a cue and STILL stalls, the agent escalates the ORDER of the impasse and changes its mind FUNDAMENTALLY about the approach. Ladder: order2=change the METHOD (re-bind a different operator), order3=change the FRAMING (decompose into a sub-axis), order4=change the TOOLS (author a NEW faculty — consumed by the self-extend reflex), order5=re-PRIORITISE (deprioritise, shift the frontier, return later), order6=RETHINK THE SELF APPROACH (the whole way it tackles this class of problem may be wrong — route to the reflective self-faculty). Keyed ONLY on the generic investigation machinery (CapabilityAxis/Operator/investigated_by/mf_stall/saturation/order) — NO domain terms — so it applies to ANY world. THE CLIMB IS CONFIDENCE-DRIVEN, not a timer: each rung ACTS ONCE, then the agent TRIES it; confidence = the axis's saturation (how well the current approach measures). The order climbs when the axis is BELOW TARGET (saturation < 0.95) and has PLATEAUED (mf_stall >= 4, now a PATIENCE counter reset on every real gain) — settling below target is no longer a victory. The escalation RESOLVES only at the GOAL (saturation >= 0.95). (The agent's escalation-policy fix, ask_jabberwock_escalation: the old 0.4 line declared victory at 40%-of-target and left plateaued-below-target axes never reaching order-4 authoring.)

microtheory.name: impasse_escalation
microtheory.description: taught-and-still-stalling -> escalate the order -> method/framing/tools/priority/self, climbing only while NOT confident the current approach works. Domain-agnostic.

rules.name: escalate_open
rules.comment: STALL-OF-STALLS: an axis already TAUGHT a cue that STILL stalls (mf_stall >= 4) and is not already escalating -> open an order-2 escalation (acted_order=1, the cue WAS order-1) and mark the current operator TRIED so order-2 re-binds to a different one.

effects.note: taught a cue and still stalling — escalate the approach; resolved by the ladder (confidence-driven), not the teacher.

rules.name: order2_change_method
rules.comment: ORDER 2 (change the METHOD): re-bind to a DIFFERENT operator FOR THE SAME CAPABILITY (same metric as the stalled op), applies in the world, NOT in the axis's `tried` set. Acts once (acted_order<2), resets mf_stall for a fresh confidence trial. The same-metric guard stops a stalled recognise axis being re-bound to a segment faculty that trivially 'succeeds' (continuous_purity=1.0) and falsely saturates it, masking the wall; when no same-metric alternative exists the climb proceeds to order-4 authoring.

rules.name: order3_reframe
rules.comment: ORDER 3 (change the FRAMING): REQUEST a finer decomposition of the stuck capability -- it does NOT mint an axis (the agent's own dedup fix, ask_jabberwock_dedup). The old version cloned the parent: it minted a sub-axis with capability_keys COPIED verbatim from the parent + subskill:1.0, an identity-duplicate of the very hill it was stuck on, which then out-ranked the parent (fresh sat=0.0) and fragmented investigation. order2 already re-binds the method and order4 authors a tool, so a same-capability sibling is never meaningful. Reframe now acts on the EXISTING axis: lay a needs_decomposition request, refresh shortfall + reset mf_stall so its confidence trial continues, and flag `reframed` (once-guard). The genuinely-distinct sub-axes come ONLY from ground_hint_to_investigation grounding a real teacher cue (keys EXTENDED with a distinguishing token), never from a copy. A consumer can honor needs_decomposition later; until then order3 is a clean no-op that climbs to order4 -- strictly better than a counterfeit hill.

rules.name: order4_self_extend
rules.comment: ORDER 4 (change the TOOLS): no existing operator and decomposition did not help -> request a NEW faculty. UNBINDS the failed operator (so nothing runs and the climb counter cannot advance on the OLD method while the new tool is being authored) and sets needs_tool; the self-extend reflex (jabberwock_authors_*) consumes it, authors a new Operator, binds the axis to it, and resets mf_stall for a fresh trial. If no authoring faculty is wired, the axis stays unbound (no measurement) and the climb proceeds to order 5.

rules.name: order5_reprioritise
rules.comment: ORDER 5 (re-PRIORITISE): set the axis aside — deprioritise it (shortfall *= 0.1) so the frontier shifts to other work; the agent returns once a prerequisite has matured. If there is no other work and it STILL fails, the climb proceeds to order 6.

rules.name: order6_rethink_self
rules.comment: ORDER 6 (RETHINK THE SELF APPROACH): even setting it aside did not help and it is unavoidable -> the agent's WHOLE approach to this class of problem may be wrong. Mint a self_rethink Impasse routed to the agent (rethinking edge) + the reflective self-faculty reflex consumes it to re-examine how the agent is organised/shaped and re-derive its approach. The deepest, terminal rung.

rules.name: escalation_climb_low_confidence
rules.comment: THE PLATEAU-DRIVEN CLIMB (the agent's escalation-policy fix, ask_jabberwock_escalation): raise the order by one when the axis is BELOW TARGET (saturation < 0.95) AND has PLATEAUED -- mf_stall >= 4 measurements with no improvement (mf_stall is now a PATIENCE counter in bank_measurement_to_axis: reset to 0 on a real saturation gain > sat_best+0.02, else incremented). The old saturation<0.4 gate declared victory at 40%-of-target and left axes stably below target un-escalated (recognition stuck at sat 0.80, never authored). A still-improving axis keeps zeroing its clock so it cannot reach 4 -- only a flat, below-target axis climbs toward order-4 authoring. Climbs up to order 6.

rules.name: escalation_resolve_high_confidence
rules.comment: REACHED TARGET: the axis under an open escalation reached saturation >= 0.95 (its GOAL, within 5%) -> resolve. Was 0.4 (40%-of-target = a false-victory exit that stranded below-target axes); now resolution means the goal is actually met, so a plateaued-below-target axis stays open and the plateau guard authors.
